Cameo Reference Map

Every Cameo actor with the reference unit chosen from each source, by full id and name, split into units that exist in the original games and units that do not. The bar on each chip is match confidence. HP →, speed → and cost → are the R4 synthesis targets — references plus Cameo, one vote each. Nothing here has been written to yaml.

161 originals · 709 expanded · 925 references · 514 priced by formula · 8 originals under three sources

td_gdi · 14 original, 18 expanded

Originals · 14

These exist in OpenRA/OpenTD, so a counterpart exists in every source and all three must be present and must be the same unit. Anything short of three, or any reference that is not plainly the same unit, is a defect worth reporting.

td_gdi_grenadier
Weapon calculation details

Raw source values are not directly comparable across games. The model normalizes each source before projection; the rate below is a source-local damage/tick estimate, not a sustained gameplay DPS claim. Unknown delays remain unavailable. Reviewed nominal cycles exclude armor, splash totals, travel and upgrades. The separate travel sample uses fixed endpoints without scatter, blockers or speed modifiers. Tick calls start at the first projectile update, not the firing order; seconds depend on game speed. Unmodeled guided/custom projectiles remain unavailable, and conditional slots are not summed.

Ordinary Air gives 4000 damage (80 per tick); AirSmall gives 7000 (140 per tick). The selected nominal reference uses ordinary Air, matching the declared Air-only comparison scenario; the unequal alternative remains visible and is not summed. Base ground Dragon and transport passenger slots are separate weapons, not extra simultaneous primary damage. Targets with overlapping tags, off-center falloff, clip rearming, popup/firing animation, movement, other weapons and upgrades excluded; not sustained actor DPS.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

Per-armament references — one weapon, one vote

These actors carry more than one weapon, so a single folded number above would describe two different guns at once — which is why the weapon columns read WITHHELD for most of them. Here each armament finds its own reference weapon and gets its own target, and a source that does not carry a weapon in that role does not vote on it. = exact role match · ~ a dual-role weapon stood in. An unproven role abstains rather than voting. Air is never paired with ground. A c on a range marks a value converted from TS cells (1 cell = 1024 WDist). The reference column is projected through the same coordinates and the same frozen ruler as every other target on this page.

wc2_orcs_cannontower
Weapon calculation details

Raw source values are not directly comparable across games. The model normalizes each source before projection; the rate below is a source-local damage/tick estimate, not a sustained gameplay DPS claim. Unknown delays remain unavailable. Reviewed nominal cycles exclude armor, splash totals, travel and upgrades. The separate travel sample uses fixed endpoints without scatter, blockers or speed modifiers. Tick calls start at the first projectile update, not the firing order; seconds depend on game speed. Unmodeled guided/custom projectiles remain unavailable, and conditional slots are not summed.
